title: VRUN: Vaults of Obsolete Code music test (MS-DOS)
description: A spinoff MUSIC TEST player (modelled on CTW NES's AudioPlayer): the game's real sound driver, included unchanged, every music track, one FL TEST slot (00: a song from an FL Studio project via BrokenDev/tools/music/flp/musictest/build-vaults-dos-mt.ps1; a silent placeholder here), looping, per-channel mute (1-9) / solo (F1-F9) from the keyboard with the channel state on screen, song number and name on screen. A separate build target (musictest/build_mt.ps1): the game build is byte-identical.

toolchain: Open Watcom 2.0 (wcc386/wcl386, wlink, DOS/32A), NASM 3.02, Python 3: C:\BrokenNes-tools\dos (env.ps1)

steps.name: build
steps.note: build_mt.ps1: wcl386 on musictest/v_mt_dos.c (includes src/voc_sound.c unchanged, its PSG bytes filtered for mute/solo), v_mt_tab.c, mt_ui.c, mt_dos.c, the FL slot (mt_fl_placeholder.c or FruityHost flp-vocdos's C), src/dos/dos_opl.c and the songs (src/music/gg): build/mt/VMT.EXE.

run.note: Up/Down pick, Enter/Space play (loops), 1-4 mute pulse 1 / pulse 2 / wave / noise, F1-F4 solo, 0 all on, S stop, Esc quit. Real hardware: T:\BrokenDev\Releases\VRUN_Vaults_DOS_MusicTest (EXE + VRUN-DOS floppy).

scenarios.why: FreeDOS boots the player: the song list (00 FL TEST, 01-11 the songs with the tracks that use them) and the 4 channels are drawn

verify.note: Mute / solo and every song are checked by the game repo's MT.TXT script (musictest/mt_ui.h: '<frame> play|mute|solo|clear|stop|quit [n]' -> MT.OUT with the chip writes, their hash and the key-ons per channel, SCREEN.TXT) on the x86 console (Workshop --x86boot with the script on the disk). The placeholder FL slot is silent, so the power-on song has no sound (no audio expectation).

knownIssues: The FL TEST slot is a silent placeholder in this build; build-vaults-dos-mt.ps1 -Flp x.flp [-AsGb] puts a song there (the Vaults back end plays Game Boy instances only: a NES-composed .flp needs -AsGb).
